title: The tomb
place: inside the tomb chamber, behind the prayer-niche wall, under the dome.

quiz.q: Who is buried in this tomb?
options: Nobody. Feedback: "His body was never found."

lineTags.1: Sultan Hasan's body was never found; he was never buried here: Wikipedia
lineTags.2: Marble panelling and the painted wooden Throne Verse inscription: Wikipedia
lineTags.3: Wooden muqarnas pendentives, painted and gilded: Wikipedia
lineTags.4: Stage act, only if the room is quiet. Unverified on site: how long the dome answers
lineTags.5: 33 days to his killing: al-Maqrizi, Khitat. Yalbugha al-Umari was Hasan's own mamluk and amir majlis; commander of the army only after Hasan's death: Wikipedia, after Van Steenbergen. The ride against Yalbugha: al-Maqrizi's biography of Hasan in Herz 1899; Wikipedia
lineTags.6: Dramatised; the escape and the rout are in al-Maqrizi's biography of Hasan (Herz 1899). Yalbugha is seen from behind only
lineTags.7: He hid in the house of the hajib Ibn al-Azkashi: al-Maqrizi's biography of Hasan in Herz's French. The whispered words are dramatised
lineTags.8: Dramatised: the whisper is invented. Hasan's flight, hiding and killing: al-Maqrizi (via Herz 1899); Wikipedia
lineTags.9: Dramatised: the whisper is invented. Hasan's flight, hiding and killing: al-Maqrizi (via Herz 1899); Wikipedia
lineTags.11: 'His trace was lost forever, despite the searches of his servants': Herz's French of al-Maqrizi's biography (Arabic not yet checked); Ibn Hajar's rival version not merged; body never found: Wikipedia
lineTags.12: His two young sons in the tomb; the egg-shaped wooden dome replaced in 1671: Wikipedia
lineTags.14: The cenotaph (1384) behind a wooden screen; his two young sons buried here; he never was: Wikipedia, after Behrens-Abouseif
lineTags.15: A mausoleum behind the qibla wall, found in no other Mamluk religious building: Wikipedia
